jokes.text: Monica says 'Keep your panties on' as an idiom. Then catches herself, looking at Chandler.
jokes.setup: Monica uses the common idiom 'keep your panties on'
jokes.punchline: The idiom lands differently because Chandler is literally in panties — Monica's pause as she realizes the phrase is a callback beat
jokes.explanation: Clever double-meaning moment. The idiom becomes literal in context. The reaction beat of Monica catching herself is the punchline. Economy is near-perfect.

jokes.text: Joey announces he got a part in Outbreak 2 as 'dying on a gurney' after a virus victim called in sick
jokes.setup: Joey reports career news from the film set
jokes.punchline: He's playing a virus victim who called in sick — a sick virus victim called in sick
jokes.explanation: Funny recursive logic — the virus victim calling in sick. Joey's delight at 'dying on a gurney' as a career achievement is nicely in-character.

jokes.text: Looks like we made it... [Barry Manilow plays as Marcel sings along]
jokes.setup: Ross and Marcel have an awkward reunion on set; Marcel had seemed indifferent
jokes.punchline: Barry Manilow's 'Looks Like We Made It' begins playing — apparently Marcel's doing — as a sentimental reunion song that's also an absurdly melodramatic choice for the moment
jokes.explanation: Marcel having a preferred sentimental song and the ability to deploy it is a great sustained absurdist gag. Barry Manilow as a monkey's chosen reunion anthem is a perfectly specific, funny choice. The visual of a capuchin monkey swaying to 'Looks Like We Made It' is strong physical comedy.

jokes.text: I'm sorry. It has work between you and me. Or you and me. / Drew was very disappointed.
jokes.setup: Van Damme appears to be apologizing or clarifying something about the threesome situation
jokes.punchline: The callback to Drew Barrymore's disappointment at the threesome not happening is the punchline — implying it was a real plan that fell through
jokes.explanation: A good callback button to the threesome subplot. 'Drew was very disappointed' confirms she was genuinely in — making the situation funnier in retrospect. The broken English adds to the comic effect.

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'I think I want to write a song about all this. Except one of the strings on my guitar is broken. Chandler, can I borrow your G-string?' Chandler: '—How long have you been waiting to say that?' Phoebe: 'About 20 minutes!'
jokes.setup: Phoebe says she needs to borrow a guitar G-string
jokes.punchline: Chandler immediately recognizes 'G-string' as a panty-pun (given he's wearing a thong); Phoebe reveals she timed the joke deliberately — acknowledging the joke as a joke
jokes.explanation: Brilliant episode button. The G-string double entendre is set up by Chandler's panty situation, and Phoebe's 'About 20 minutes!' reveals she's been engineering this joke for the entire scene — making her the funniest meta-comedian in the room. The structure is perfect: real request + double meaning + acknowledgment of the joke's construction. One of the episode's best.

jokes.text: Chandler, can I borrow your G-string? / How long you been waiting to say that? / About 20 minutes!
jokes.setup: Phoebe needs to borrow Chandler's guitar G-string (a string on the instrument)
jokes.punchline: Chandler calls her out on the obvious double entendre setup; Phoebe admits she's been sitting on this joke for 20 minutes — she was waiting for the right moment
jokes.explanation: An outstanding callback joke and meta-comedy moment. The structure is layered: the G-string pun is the surface joke, Chandler catching it is the second beat, but Phoebe's admission of a 20-minute wait is the best part — she pre-planned the timing of her own joke. It's character comedy, wordplay, and meta-comedy simultaneously. 'About 20 minutes' is delivered with perfect Phoebe sincerity. One of the episode's top jokes.

jokes.text: Joey's failed acting scene — repeated takes: 'Can't you see what's going on here? This man is dying!' Cut. Repeat. Cut. Repeat. Final take: 'This man is dead!'
jokes.setup: Joey films his Outbreak 2 scene — a dramatic line about a dying man
jokes.punchline: After multiple failed takes of 'This man is dying!', Joey accidentally upgrades the line to 'This man is dead!' — the patient apparently perished between takes
jokes.explanation: Excellent tag joke for the episode. The escalating flubbed takes build through repetition, and 'This man is dead!' as the final variation is a perfect organic punchline — Joey has accidentally improved the script by flubbing it. The escalation structure is textbook. Also ends on a kid saying 'Mommy!' which adds a final absurdist beat.

tmdb_overview: Ross goes to visit Marcel, his monkey, while on a trip to California. Joey gets his first fan letter and ends up dating the woman. Phoebe is asked to sing for the children at the library, but their parents are horrified by her lyrics.
insight: Super Bowl episode lands 58 jokes in 45 minutes but underperforms impact expectations at 76.5.
